summary:
What we developed: We built EarthEcho, a modern, interactive web application (Vite + React + Tailwind CSS) that functions as an "Earth Jukebox." It translates NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) visual data—such as night lights evolution, ISS lightning events, and GEDI forest canopy heights—into dynamic, real-time soundscapes.   

How it addresses the challenge: The project directly tackles the Earth Observation Sonification challenge by bridging a critical gap in Earth science communication. While NASA provides extraordinary visual datasets, relying exclusively on sight limits accessibility. EarthEcho converts visual frames and data parameters into multi-sensory audio, transforming complex planetary data into an intuitive auditory experience.
  
 Why it is important: EarthEcho champions accessibility by opening up Earth science to blind and low-vision users. Furthermore, by blending data translation with musicality, it helps reveal subtle environmental patterns and fosters a deeper emotional connection to our changing planet.
details:
Working

  • What it does: EarthEcho is a modern, interactive web application (built using Vite, React, and Tailwind CSS) that functions as an "Earth Jukebox". It translates NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) visual data—such as urban night lights, ISS lightning flashes, and GEDI forest canopy heights—into dynamic, real-time soundscapes.
  • How it works: The application processes visual frames and data parameters from NASA's EIC and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) datasets, mapping visual elements like brightness, color spectrums, and pixel density to audio parameters such as pitch, rhythm, tempo, and instrumentation. Users can select and experience these visualizations alongside their corresponding interactive audio stories.

Benefits

  • Multi-Sensory Engagement: Bridges the gap between purely visual Earth science and auditory perception, allowing users to experience environmental data in an entirely new dimension.
  • Pattern Recognition: Translating data into sound helps reveal subtle environmental patterns and shifts that might easily be missed by the naked eye alone.
  • Emotional Resonance: Combines scientific data mapping with artistic rulesets to foster a deeper emotional connection to our changing planet.

Intended impact

  • Universal Accessibility: Directly addresses a major gap in Earth science communication by making complex planetary data accessible to blind and low-vision users who are typically excluded by visual-only dashboards.
  • Environmental Awareness: Inspires broader public curiosity and climate awareness by turning intricate Earth telemetry into compelling, immersive soundscapes that communicate planetary urgency and beauty.

Coding languages, hardware, or software used

  • Frontend Framework: React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Hosting & Deployment: GitHub Pages automated via GitHub Actions ([https://lakshmikrishna-hue.github.io/EarthEcho/](https://lakshmikrishna-hue.github.io/EarthEcho/)).
  • Data Sources: NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) datasets—specifically focusing on night lights evolution (2012–2023), ISS lightning events, and GEDI forest heights.

Creative Aspect

  • Turning Sight into Sound: Instead of treating NASA data as static charts or videos, EarthEcho turns datasets into a living, breathing musical instrument (the "Earth Jukebox").
  • Balancing Science and Artistry: Rather than letting raw data sound like chaotic noise, the application applies artistic rulesets and harmonies to ensure the generated soundscapes remain pleasant, emotional, and musically engaging while staying entirely faithful to the underlying science.

Factors considered

  • UX & Accessibility: Focused heavily on how intuitively a user can navigate the interface and experience the transition from visual imagery to audio, keeping accessibility front and center.
  • Technical Reliability: Ensured a seamless deployment pipeline with proper path configurations (base: '/EarthEcho/') so that judges can easily access and test the live web application without broken links or missing assets.
